nodes.label: Abstract
nodes.description: A short self-contained summary of the problem, approach, and main findings placed at the start of the paper.

nodes.label: Introduction
nodes.description: The opening section that motivates the problem, states the research questions or contributions, and outlines the paper.

nodes.label: Related work
nodes.description: A survey of prior literature that positions the paper against existing approaches.

nodes.label: Background
nodes.description: Preliminary definitions, notation, and technical context the reader needs before the method, distinct from the review of competing work.

nodes.label: Method
nodes.description: The description of the proposed approach, model, algorithm, or study design, including how data were collected or processed.

nodes.label: Experiments
nodes.description: The experimental setup: datasets, baselines, metrics, implementation details, and evaluation protocol, before the numbers are discussed.

nodes.label: Results
nodes.description: The reported outcomes of the experiments or analyses, with tables, figures, and their direct interpretation.

nodes.label: Discussion
nodes.description: An interpretation of the results that examines implications, explanations, and comparison with expectations beyond the raw numbers.

nodes.label: Limitations
nodes.description: An explicit statement of the weaknesses, assumptions, threats to validity, and scope boundaries of the work.

nodes.label: Conclusion
nodes.description: The closing summary of what was shown, with future directions.

nodes.label: Acknowledgements
nodes.description: Thanks to funders, colleagues, and reviewers, including funding statements and author contributions.

nodes.label: References
nodes.description: The bibliography listing the cited works.

nodes.label: Appendix
nodes.description: Supplementary material placed after the main text, such as extra proofs, tables, derivations, and additional experiments.
